examples.en: The road was blocked by a sudden downpour.
I was surprised when the company raised prices all of a sudden.
It was a surprise announcement, so there was no time to prepare.
It was so sudden that it was hard to respond.
Even when asked a surprise question, I answered calmly.
Citizens were startled by the policy announced out of the blue.

explain: 관형사로 분류되지만 실제로는 '기습적인', '기습적으로'처럼 활용해서 써요. '갑자기'와 달리 상대가 준비하지 못한 때에 하는 느낌이 있어요. 뉴스에서 '기습적 인상', '기습적 폭우' 같은 말로 보여요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 꾸미는 꼴로, 예상 못 한 때에 갑자기라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies a verb; means suddenly, when least expected.

phrases.en: Everyone was flustered by the sudden announcement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 준비 없이 갑자기 한 발표를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to an announcement made without warning.

phrases.en: I couldn't answer the surprise question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예상하지 못한 질문을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a question you did not expect.

explain_en: Although it is classified as a determiner, it is actually used with endings like '기습적인' and '기습적으로'. Unlike '갑자기', it implies doing something when the other side is unprepared. In the news you see phrases like '기습적 인상' (a surprise hike) and '기습적 폭우'.

en: to be mighty; to be powerful

examples.en: That team is really formidable.

examples.ko: 막강한 힘을 가진 회사가 시장을 이끌어요.
examples.en: A powerful company leads the market.
The opposing player was too strong.

examples.ko: 막강한 군대를 가진 나라는 많지 않아요.
examples.en: Not many countries have a mighty army.

examples.ko: 이 게임은 캐릭터가 막강해서 이기기 쉬워요.
examples.en: In this game the character is so strong that winning is easy.
His influence is known to be enormous.

explain: '강하다'보다 훨씬 세서 맞서기 어렵다는 느낌이에요. 힘·권력·팀·군대·영향력처럼 규모가 큰 대상에 어울려요. 작은 물건이 단단하다고 할 때는 '튼튼하다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 그 나라는 막강한 군사력을 가지고 있어요.
phrases.en: That country has mighty military power.
phrases.nuance_ko: '막강한' 뒤에 힘, 군사력, 권력 같은 큰 말이 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: 막강한 is followed by big words like power, military strength, or authority.

phrases.en: Our team's attack was really powerful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 경기나 일에서 어느 쪽이 아주 셌다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a side was very strong in a past game or event.

phrases.en: That company is not as mighty as it used to be.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 예전보다 힘이 약해졌다고 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form can say that something has become weaker than before.

explain_en: Much stronger than 강하다, with a sense that it is hard to stand against. It fits big things such as power, authority, teams, armies and influence. For a small sturdy object, use 튼튼하다 instead.

en: being unsuitable; being unfit; being inappropriate

examples.en: It was judged unsuitable in the inspection.
They say this water is not fit to drink.
The documents are unsuitable, so I have to submit them again.

examples.ko: 어린이에게 부적합한 내용이라 영화를 못 봤어요.
examples.en: The content was inappropriate for children, so I couldn't watch the movie.

examples.ko: 식품 안전 검사에서 부적합으로 나온 제품은 팔 수 없어요.
examples.en: Products that fail the food safety inspection can't be sold.

examples.ko: 그 일은 제 성격에 부적합하다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think that job doesn't suit my personality.

explain: 반대말은 '적합'이고, 검사나 심사에서 '부적합 판정'처럼 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '안 맞아요'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요. '부적격'은 사람의 자격에 주로 쓰고, 부적합은 조건이나 기준에 안 맞을 때 써요.

phrases.en: This place is unsuitable for children to play in.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부적합'을 형용사처럼 써서 어떤 일에 맞지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 부적합 like an adjective to say something does not suit a purpose.

phrases.example: 이 요리에 부적합한 재료를 쓰면 맛이 없어요.
phrases.en: If you use unsuitable ingredients for this dish, it won't taste good.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부적합한 + 명사'로 기준에 맞지 않는 것을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The 'unsuitable + noun' pattern for things that fail to meet a standard.

phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '부적합'을 쉽게 바꿔 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy everyday way to say 부적합 in conversation.

explain_en: The opposite is '적합', and it often appears in inspections and reviews as '부적합 판정'. In everyday talk people usually say '안 맞아요'. '부적격' is mostly about a person's qualifications, while 부적합 is about not meeting conditions or standards.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 연결의 불안정성 때문에 자주 꺼져요.
examples.en: This app often shuts down because of its unstable connection.
The instability of the economy is growing.
Many young people worry about job insecurity.
They ran an inspection to check the bridge's instability.

examples.ko: 시장의 불안정성에 대비해서 돈을 모아 두고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm saving money to prepare for market instability.

examples.ko: 이 의자는 구조의 불안정성 때문에 쉽게 흔들려요.
examples.en: This chair wobbles easily because of its unstable structure.

explain: '불안정'에 '-성'이 붙어서, 그런 성질이 있다는 점을 짚어 말할 때 써요. 경제, 고용, 시스템, 구조처럼 설명하는 글에 자주 나오고, 일상에서는 '불안정하다', '흔들리다'를 써요. 반의어는 '안정성'이에요.

phrases.en: The instability of the market is growing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흔들리고 위험한 정도가 더 심해진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the degree of wobbliness and risk is getting worse.

phrases.en: We replaced the equipment to reduce the server's instability.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 되는 흔들림을 적게 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making the problematic instability smaller.

phrases.example: 고용의 불안정성 때문에 젊은 사람들이 걱정해요.
phrases.en: Young people are worried because of job insecurity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일자리가 안정되지 않은 문제를 설명하는 글에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in writing about the problem of unstable employment.

explain_en: With '-성' added to '불안정', it points out that something has this quality. It often appears in explanatory writing about the economy, employment, systems and structures, while daily speech uses '불안정하다' or '흔들리다'. The opposite is '안정성'.

examples.ko: 이 구역은 사고가 잦아서 요주의 지역이에요.
examples.en: This area has frequent accidents, so it's a zone to be careful in.

examples.ko: 그 거래처는 요주의 대상이라 계약 전에 꼭 확인해요.
examples.en: That client needs extra caution, so we always check before signing a contract.
This file is marked as requiring caution.
Nurses check frequently on patients who need special watching.
This mountain road needs extra care during the rainy season.

examples.ko: 열에 약한 물건이라 상자에 요주의 표시가 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: The item is sensitive to heat, so the box has a caution label on it.

explain: '요주의 지역', '요주의 인물', '요주의 대상'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여 쓰는 경우가 많고 안내문, 서류, 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '조심해야 해요', '주의가 필요해요'라고 풀어서 말해요.

phrases.en: That person is someone to watch out for at the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조심해서 지켜봐야 하는 사람을 가리키며, 보통 부정적인 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to someone who must be watched carefully, usually with a negative tone.

phrases.en: You need to be careful on this road at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '요주의' 대신 풀어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday way to say what 'yojuui' means.

phrases.en: The stairs are slippery, so you have to be careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉽고 부드럽게 주의를 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, softer way to give a warning.

explain_en: It is often placed before another noun, as in '요주의 지역', '요주의 인물' or '요주의 대상', and appears in notices, documents and news. In everyday talk people say '조심해야 해요' or '주의가 필요해요' instead.

en: to be risky; to be perilous; to be critical

examples.en: The bridge is old, so it is precarious to cross.
That company is in a precarious situation right now.

examples.ko: 아이가 높은 난간에 위태하게 서 있었어요.
examples.en: The child was standing precariously on the high railing.
My health was in danger, so I was admitted to the hospital.
The patient whose life had been in danger woke up.

examples.ko: 경기가 나빠져서 가게가 위태할 것 같아요.
examples.en: The economy got worse, so the shop looks like it is in danger.

explain: '위험하다'는 다치거나 문제가 생길 가능성이 있다는 뜻이고, '위태하다'는 곧 무너질 것처럼 아슬아슬한 상태에 써요. 말할 때는 '위태롭다'가 더 흔하고 뜻은 거의 같아요.

phrases.example: 그 다리는 너무 낡아서 위태해 보여요.
phrases.en: That bridge is so old that it looks precarious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습으로 판단할 때 '-아/어 보이다'를 붙여요. 말할 때는 '위태로워 보여요'가 더 흔하고 뜻은 거의 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -아/어 보이다 to judge by appearance. In speech, 위태로워 보여요 is more common and means almost the same.

phrases.en: Even in a critical situation, he stayed calm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 활용형이에요. 상황, 처지, 목숨과 자주 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form before a noun. Often goes with situation, position, or life.

phrases.example: 지금은 우리 회사 상황이 위태하지 않아요.
phrases.en: Our company's situation isn't critical right now.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, saying the situation is not on the brink.

explain_en: '위험하다' says something could cause harm, while '위태하다' describes a shaky, about-to-collapse state. In speech '위태롭다' is more common and means almost the same.
